evidence: gpt-oss-120b uses an integer bitset and adjacency lists; glm-5 uses `adj = [set() ...]` and iterates the graph lexicographically
affordance_in_statement: Each of the next m lines contains two integers u and v — a pair of workers who have a mutual grievance. Each grievance is listed at most once.
removal_suggestion: Make the order of grievance records semantically relevant: require the three grievance records for the selected triangle to occupy three consecutive input lines, while retaining the existing pairwise-grievance and lexicographic requirements. Update the guarantee to promise that at least one such triangle exists.

survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The input describes pairs of workers with mutual grievances, with each grievance listed at most once.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Enumerates a, b, and c with nested loops, leading to cubic worst-case work and TLE.

recommended_edit: Add the requirement that the three grievance records corresponding to the chosen triangle must be three consecutive lines in the input, and guarantee that at least one such triangle exists. This defeats both surviving solutions because they discard edge positions while constructing adjacency structures.
